newsitem.title: CHINA: China state sector ripe for reform not privatising.
newsitem.headline: China state sector ripe for reform not privatising.

text.p: China said on Monday its increasing effort in state enterprise reform did not hail the beginning of large-scale privatisation.
Chen Qingtai, vice-minister of the State Economic and Trade Commission, rejected privatisation of state-owned enterprises as part of the reform plan, the China Securities newspaper said.

"Listing state-owned enterprises or employee share-holding are some of the directions taken to boost state sector reform, but putting a figure on state assets for private individuals is not a viable way," the newspaper quoted Chen as saying.
State sector reforms are aimed at shaking up lethargic state-owned firms as China shifts towards a market economy from state planning.

"The leasing, transfer or sale of small firms is allowed, but this does not suggest China wants to redistribute its assets among its 1.2 billion people, much less suggest it will implement privatisation," he said.
Addressing an international conference, Chen said time was ripe for speeding up market reforms in the state sector with stock listings and more foreign investments, it said.
No further details on these measures were given.
